name: source
summary: Runs a file of commands in the current shell.
description: Shell builtin, also written as a single dot (. file). Unlike ./script.sh, which runs in a new process, source reads the file in the current shell: the variables, aliases and functions it defines stay available afterwards. This is what you do after editing ~/.bashrc, or to activate a Python virtual environment.

examples.explanation: Applies the changes to ~/.bashrc right away, without opening a new terminal.
Activates a Python virtual environment in the current terminal.
Loads variables from a configuration file.

dangerNote: source runs everything in the file with your permissions, in your shell. Only use it on files whose contents you know.
